title: Localized generic multiplication is universally injective after flattening
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative integral domain with fraction field $K$, the localization at all nonzero elements. Let $B$ be a commutative $A$-algebra, $m\geq0$, and $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in B$. Define $\mu:B\to B^{\oplus m}$ by $b\mapsto(g_ib)_i$, and let $M=B^{\oplus m}/\operatorname{im}\mu$ be its cokernel. Suppose $\mu_K:B\otimes_AK\to(B\otimes_AK)^{\oplus m}$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $0\ne a\in A$, and suppose $B_a$ and $M_a$ are flat as $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], with localization at the powers of the image of $a$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Then the canonical map $B_a\to B\otimes_AK$ is injective and the canonical quotient map gives a short exact sequence $0\to B_a\xrightarrow{\mu_a}B_a^{\oplus m}\to M_a\to0$. For every $A$-module $N$, the map $\mathrm{id}_N\otimes\mu_a:N\otimes_AB_a\to N\otimes_AB_a^{\oplus m}$ is injective. In particular, for every commutative $A$-algebra $C$ in which the image of $a$ is a unit, the map $\mu_C:B\otimes_AC\to(B\otimes_AC)^{\oplus m}$, $b\mapsto((g_i\otimes1)b)_i$, is injective. No finite type, finite presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Let $q:B^{\oplus m}\to M$ be the quotient by $\operatorname{im}\mu$. By its definition, $B\xrightarrow{\mu}B^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{q}M\to0$ is exact, without an assertion of injectivity at $B$. Localize this sequence as a sequence of $A$-modules at $T=\{1,a,a^2,\ldots\}$. The cited exactness theorem gives exactness at the middle term and surjectivity onto $M_a$ (apply it also to $B^{\oplus m}\to M\to0$). Identify $T^{-1}(B^{\oplus m})$ with $B_a^{\oplus m}$ by $(b_i)_i/a^n\mapsto(b_i/a^n)_i$: a finite tuple of fractions has a common denominator, and the fraction equality criterion proves injectivity by taking the maximum of finitely many exponents. This includes $m=0$, where both modules are zero. The localized maps are $\mu_a(b/a^n)=(g_ib/a^n)_i$ and $q_a((b_i)_i/a^n)=q((b_i)_i)/a^n$. Thus $B_a\xrightarrow{\mu_a}B_a^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{q_a}M_a\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact), applied to the cokernel sequence in Tag 0573

proof.text: Put $D=B_a$ and $B_K=B\otimes_AK$. Since $A$ is a domain, $A\to K$ is injective. Flatness of $D$ and the cited tensor-injectivity lemma show that $D\otimes_AA\to D\otimes_AK$ is injective. The mutually inverse maps $D\otimes_AA\to D$, $d\otimes r\mapsto rd$, and $d\mapsto d\otimes1$ identify this map with $d\mapsto d\otimes1$. There is an isomorphism $\alpha:D\otimes_AK\to B_K$, $(b/a^n)\otimes k\mapsto b\otimes a^{-n}k$, with inverse $b\otimes k\mapsto(b/1)\otimes k$. These formulas respect the localization relation: $a^t(a^rb-a^nc)=0$ gives equal tensors after multiplication by the invertible scalar $a^{-(t+n+r)}$. They respect the tensor relations by bilinearity; the composites are the identity since $(b/a^n)\otimes k=(b/1)\otimes a^{-n}k$. Hence the canonical map $j:D\to B_K$, $b/a^n\mapsto b\otimes a^{-n}$, is injective.

source.place: Tag 0573, torsion-freeness and embedding into the generic fibre; tensor formulas as in Tags 00CX and 00DK

proof.text: For $d=b/a^n\in B_a$ the equality $\mu_K(j(d))=(j(g_id))_i$ holds coordinatewise, since both sides have $i$th entry $g_ib\otimes a^{-n}$. If $\mu_a(d)=0$, then $\mu_K(j(d))=0$. The assumed injectivity of $\mu_K$ gives $j(d)=0$, and step 2 gives $d=0$. Therefore $\mu_a$ is injective. Together with step 1 this proves the asserted short exact sequence with its specified quotient map. This argument also applies to the empty tuple: its generic injectivity forces $j(d)=0$ for every $d$, so $B_a=0$.

source.place: Tag 0573, the argument that the generic kernel vanishes in the torsion-free algebra

proof.text: Apply the flat-quotient tensor-injectivity theorem to the short exact sequence from step 3 over the ring $A$. Its quotient is exactly $M_a$, flat as an $A$-module by hypothesis. For every $A$-module $N$ it gives injectivity of $\mathrm{id}_N\otimes\mu_a:N\otimes_AB_a\to N\otimes_AB_a^{\oplus m}$. The theorem does not require $N$ to be flat or finitely generated.

Let $C$ be an $A$-algebra and let $u$ be the image of $a$, a unit in $C$. Apply step 4 with $N=C$. The symmetry $c\otimes d\mapsto d\otimes c$ (its own inverse, by the tensor relations), and the cited finite-product tensor isomorphism identify its target with $(B_a\otimes_AC)^{\oplus m}$. Define $\beta:B_a\otimes_AC\to B\otimes_AC$ by $(b/a^n)\otimes c\mapsto b\otimes u^{-n}c$. Its inverse is $b\otimes c\mapsto(b/1)\otimes c$. The localization relation is respected because a relation killed by $a^t$ becomes zero after multiplying by the unit $u^{-t}$; bilinearity gives maps on tensors. Their composites are the identity: $(b/a^n)\otimes c=(b/1)\otimes u^{-n}c$. Under $\beta$ and its coordinatewise product, the tensor of $\mu_a$ sends $b\otimes c$ to $(g_ib\otimes c)_i$, precisely multiplication by $(g_i\otimes1)_i$. Thus the injectivity in step 4 is the required injectivity of $\mu_C$. The construction allows the zero algebra $C$ and uses no finiteness or Noetherian assumptions.
